infra-context · map

Infra map

How the system under test is built, run and deployed, and the budgets it must hold.

Overview

Bunkai (repo upex-bunkai-tms) is a single Next.js 15 App Router application that serves both the UI (React Server Components + client components) and a REST API (app/api/v1/* route handlers). There is no separate backend service: it is a modular monolith deployed serverless on Vercel, backed by Supabase (PostgreSQL 16, Auth, Realtime) with per-workspace multi-tenancy enforced by Row Level Security. Error monitoring and analytics integrations named in the legacy SRS are NOT present, and its R2 object storage was replaced in practice by Supabase Storage for workspace exports (see discovery-gaps); Stripe billing, Resend transactional email and a Jira import worker ARE present and were absent from the legacy docs.

Data flow

Browser or agent → HTTPS → Next.js route handler (withApiHandler) → principal resolution → supabase-js client (RLS-scoped) → Supabase PostgreSQL. Writes that trigger side effects fan out: billing checkout calls Stripe before returning a hosted URL (plan flips asynchronously via the Stripe webhook), the daily digest cron (POST /api/v1/admin/send-digest, Vercel cron, Bearer CRON_SECRET) sends Resend emails, and the Jira import worker (app/api/v1/imports) calls the Atlassian REST API. Run/step state lives in the database; the legacy SRS's Supabase Realtime push path was not confirmed in current code (discovery-gaps).

Auth flow (sequence)

  1. User opens a protected route (/home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity).
  2. middleware.ts builds a Supabase SSR client from NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL + NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, refreshes the session cookie via supabase.auth.getUser(), and redirects anonymous users to /login?next={path}.
  3. Login options (server wrappers around supabase-js): password (POST /api/v1/auth/signin → signInWithPassword), magic link / email OTP (POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link → signInWithOtp), OAuth GitHub/Google (/auth/oauth/[provider] → signInWithOAuth).
  4. Session lives in Supabase auth cookies; API calls from the browser use the cookie rail (SSR client lib/supabase/server.ts).
  5. CLI / AI-agent traffic uses the second rail: Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_… personal access tokens verified against access_tokens + access_token_secrets (hash lookup, prefix index); SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET mints a user JWT so RLS auth.uid() applies identically to both rails (lib/api/principal.ts, lib/api/user-jwt.ts).
  6. Some routes declare a cookie-only posture and structurally reject Bearer PATs (e.g. active-workspace switch, membership deletion) — enforced by the gateway, not per-handler.

Concrete request/payload details for framework adaptation live in the backend section.

Database (architecture level)

One store: Supabase PostgreSQL 16. Access is exclusively through supabase-js (browser, SSR, admin clients) plus SQL RPC functions; no ORM. Authorization truth is Postgres RLS (policies on every table carrying workspace_id, helpers in 0005_rls_helpers.sql). Table-level detail (entities, relationships, state machines) belongs to business-data-context; this map only records the subsystem grouping: tenancy (workspaces, members, invites, access tokens), authoring (projects, modules, user stories, acceptance criteria, ATCs), execution (tests, runs, run steps), defects (bugs), integrations (imports, billing, notifications), and QA infrastructure (qa inspector role, 0085/0086 migrations).

Security architecture

  • AuthN: Supabase Auth (session cookies) + hashed personal access tokens (secrets stored in a sibling table).
  • AuthZ: RLS per workspace_id; capability scopes on PATs; owner-gated billing operations.
  • Input validation: Zod schemas shared server + client.
  • XSS: markdown rendered through react-markdown + rehype-sanitize.
  • Secrets: server-only lib/env.ts (Zod-validated, server-only import); Vercel env vars deployed, .env local.
  • CSP with nonces and numeric rate limits (100 write / 600 read per minute) appear only in legacy specs — no implementation found in the repo (discovery-gaps).

Performance hooks

No cache layer (Redis, Next.js revalidate, route caching) found in code; the health route is marked force-dynamic. Connection pooling is delegated to Supabase poolers (pooled port 6543 vs direct 5432, documented in .env.example). Numeric budgets live in the nfr-performance section as targets, not measurements.

QA relevance

  • API contract testing target: app/api/v1/* with a committed OpenAPI spec; interactive docs at /api/docs (Scalar).
  • RLS cross-workspace access attempts and cookie-vs-PAT parity are the highest-value AuthZ suites.
  • A public testability guide exists at /qa (app/qa/page.tsx, config in app/qa/qa-config.ts).
  • Auth middleware, Stripe webhook, and the cron-guarded digest route all need environment-aware test setup.

Failure impact for tests. Supabase down = everything down (auth + data). Stripe missing or down = checkout returns 503 payment_processor_unavailable; the rest of the app is designed to boot without Stripe (lazy client). Resend missing = digest sends fail per-user without crashing the app. Jira missing = import jobs fail with jira_unauthorized, not a boot error. Vercel cron absent (local dev) = digest never fires — tests must trigger the route directly with CRON_SECRET.

Legacy SRS listed Cloudflare R2 (evidence blobs), Sentry and PostHog: none of these have any client or configuration in the current codebase — see discovery-gaps.

Auth flow (concrete)

  1. Password: POST /api/v1/auth/signin {email, password} → supabase.auth.signInWithPassword → session cookies set.
  2. Magic link / OTP: POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link {email} → supabase.auth.signInWithOtp; confirm via /api/v1/auth/confirm; resend via /api/v1/auth/resend.
  3. OAuth (GitHub / Google): /auth/oauth/[provider] → supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth → callback route.
  4. Session: Supabase auth cookies; middleware.ts refreshes on every matched request; protected prefixes /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity.
  5. API machine auth: Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_… → prefix-index lookup → constant-time hash compare → scopes; user JWT minted with SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET so RLS sees auth.uid(); some routes are cookie-only.

Monitoring & rollback

No in-app APM/error-tracking SDK found (legacy Sentry/PostHog claims are unbacked). Platform-level observability is whatever the Vercel dashboard provides. Rollback = Vercel deployment rollback (prior Git SHA redeploy); no documented runbook.

CI/CD

Current state: no CI pipelines. .github/workflows/ does not exist (verified — the .github/ directory itself is absent). Delivery relies on Vercel's git integration: pushes deploy according to the Vercel project's branch settings (exact bindings unverified from the repo).

Deployment checklist (current reality)

  • Pre-deploy: bun run repo:check + bun test (manual — nothing enforces them on push).

  • Rollback: Vercel dashboard / vercel rollback to a prior deployment.
